title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Judicial Interpretations Regarding Cases Involving Guarantee Disputes and the Determination of the Mode of Suretyship Liability

articles.content_en: I. The Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning Guarantee in Cases of Disputes over Economic Contracts (Fa Fa [1994] No. 8) shall apply to guarantee dispute cases that occur after such Provisions come into force and to guarantee dispute cases of first instance and second instance that occur before such Provisions come into force but have not yet been concluded. For guarantee dispute cases where judgments or rulings have already taken legal effect before such Provisions come into force and are subject to retrial, such Provisions shall not apply. For guaranty acts and guarantee disputes that occur after the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China takes effect, the Guarantee Law and the provisions of the relevant judicial interpretations of the Guarantee Law shall apply.

II. Where a guaranty contract concluded before the Guarantee Law took effect has no agreement on or an unclear agreement on the mode of the guarantor's liability, it shall be deemed as general suretyship. If the guaranty contract explicitly stipulates that the guarantor shall assume the guaranty liability only when the debtor is unable to perform the debt, it shall be regarded as general suretyship. If the guaranty contract explicitly stipulates that the guarantor shall assume the guaranty liability when the guaranteed person fails to perform the debt, and it cannot be presumed as general suretyship liability according to the true intention of the parties when concluding the contract, it shall be regarded as joint and several suretyship.

Before this Reply comes into force, for guarantee dispute cases where judgments or rulings have already taken legal effect, if any party applies for retrial or a decision is made to retry the case according to the trial supervision procedure, this Reply shall not apply.

This is our reply.

November 23, 2002
